[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Insert Interval** [LC 57 · Insert Interval](https://leetcode.com/problems/insert-interval/){difficulty="Medium"}

The premise is stronger than @sec-int-p1-a's: `intervals` is already sorted *and* already merged. That means every interval strictly to the left of `newInterval` (end $< s$) can be copied verbatim, every interval strictly to the right (start $> e$) can be copied verbatim, and everything in between gets absorbed into a single extended block. The result is a three-phase linear walk: **copy-left, absorb-overlaps, copy-right**. A `bisect` variant locates the two boundary indices in $O(\log n)$ and splices once — the walk is $O(k)$ in the number actually absorbed.

[Solved in full in @sec-int-p1-b.]{.card-link}

:::
